speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned episodes of unresponsiveness with facial grimacing; how long do these episodes typically last, and do you lose consciousness?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Autoimmune Encephalitis (Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis). The presence of a "muddy taste" preceding episodes, combined with post-ictal confusion and complex semiology like hand gestures, is highly suggestive of autoimmune encephalitis rather than typical epilepsy or syncope.

REQUEST TEST: Anti-NMDA receptor antibodies, EEG, Lumbar_Puncture
